messages:
anya: Heads-up — during the model rollout this morning a few saved per-route views showed large telemetry regressions in token usage and p50 latency. We need a console affordance to let engineers quickly rollback the route's active model pin from the saved view if telemetry crosses a threshold. :warning:

sam: Can you paste the telemetry query or the exact signal? what's regressed and by how much?

anya: Quick probe: `select p50_latency, avg_tokens from route_metrics where route='/summarize' and model='redwood-v2' and window='24h'` — p50 up ~220ms vs pinned v1, avg tokens +15%. Not massive but enough to spike costs.

rachel: UX thought: in the saved view header show 'Active model: redwood-v2 (since 10:12) — [Rollback]' with an inline badge that appears only when a regression alert exists for that route+model. Clicking opens a confirmation modal.

mike: Backend note: current saved-query schema only stores filters/display prefs, not model pins. We'll need to extend the saved-query contract with `pinned_model` and `pin_since` (nullable) to surface this in the UI. Keep v1 reads working.

julian: Agree on schema bump. Suggest we implement saved-query schema v2 that adds `pinned_model` and `pin_metadata`. Server can present both versions for compatibility; console will prefer v2 when present.

sam: Also important: the rollback button should only be enabled if the telemetry alert meets our gating rules. We shouldn't allow rollbacks from noisy signals (low sample counts).

anya: Proposed flow: 1) telemetry alert fires for route+model pair; 2) console flags saved views that include that route with a 'regression detected' badge; 3) rollback button appears; 4) user clicks -> modal shows expected impact (delta p50, delta token cost) and requires role confirmation before kicking off a canary rollback.

mike: API sketch: `POST /api/saved_queries/:id/rollback` with body `{"target_model":"redwood-v1","mode":"canary","canary_pct":10}` returns `{ "rollout_id": 1234 }`. Endpoint will create a rollout job in routing service and write an audit log.

rachel: In the modal we should surface a small diff: 'p50 +220ms, tokens +15% (24h)'. If the rollback is a canary, show canary progress and a 'stop canary' action directly in the modal. Also link to the route ownership and docs.

julian: Routing service already supports canaries at route-level, but we need to translate saved-query -> rollout spec. Important: permissions — not every console user can roll back a route. We should restrict to `routes.manage` or `console.rollback`.

sam: Telemetry gating detail: we currently sample ~1% for low-traffic routes which is noisy. Suggest we require both a relative delta threshold and a minimum absolute sample count (min_samples=200) before enabling rollback. If below, UI should show 'insufficient data'.

mike: Edge case: saved view might include a `model_override` (a per-view temporary override) separate from route-level pinned model. We must show both: 'view override' and 'route pin'. Rollback should act on the route pin unless user explicitly wants to change the view-only override.

anya: Good call. Also we should surface when a saved view was created against a different model (help users reason about drift).

rachel: UX question: should rollback be a single-click that fully reverts route pin or always require canary? I think default to canary (10%) with a one-click advanced toggle to do immediate full rollback for owners.

julian: Technical: routing service API accepts rollout specs; we can reuse that and store a pointer to the saved-query in the rollout metadata so audit/traceability is easy. Also ensure rollback via console records a trace id that telemetry can attach to.

sam: Ops: add a gating alert that notifies route owners and the rollout team when a rollback is initiated from console. We should also add a 'why' field in the rollout metadata referencing the telemetry signal id.

mike: I'll add the saved-query schema change PR (WIP). Example body for schema v2: `{"id":987654, "filters":{...}, "display_prefs":{...}, "pinned_model":"redwood-v2", "pin_since":"2024-11-07T10:12:00Z"}`. Back-compat: servers will ignore unknown keys for v1 clients.

deploy-bot: routing-service PR #1123 deployed to staging at 2024-11-07T16:00Z.

sam: One more telemetry nuance — use rolling-window aggregations (24h and 3h) to reduce false positives. Show both numbers in modal so PMs can make a call.

anya: Action items: (1) backend: saved-query schema v2 + rollback endpoint (owner: mike), (2) routing: accept rollback-triggered rollout spec and add metadata (owner: julian), (3) telemetry: implement gating with min_samples + multi-window deltas (owner: sam), (4) console UX: badge + rollback modal + canary status + ownership checks (owner: rachel), (5) perms & audit logs (owner: anya). I'll assemble an RFC doc and assign tasks.

rachel: I'll mock up the modal and header state by EOD, will include the 'insufficient data' state.

mike: PR opened for schema changes, marking WIP, linking this thread.

anya: Thanks — sync tomorrow 10:00 to align API shapes and perms.

rachel: :thumbsup:

mike: Filing follow-ups in the RFC now.
